slides.title: Alibaba Launches Qwen-Robot Series Embodied AI Large Models
slides.tldr: ALIBABA RELEASES QWEN-ROBOT EMBODIED AI MODELS
slides.highlight: Alibaba has launched the Qwen-Robot series of embodied AI large models, which is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and AI-mediated learning.

slides.title: Evaluating Large Language Models Abilities for Addressee, Turn-change, and Next Speaker Prediction in Meetings
slides.highlight: This research evaluates LLMs and multimodal LLMs on addressee detection and speaker prediction, contributing to HyECHO's focus on addressee/listener modeling and engagement in hybrid teams.

card.one_liner: LLMs outperform humans and supervised models in next speaker prediction for multi-party meetings using conversational context.
card.key_idea: A unified framework comparing supervised models, text-based LLMs, and MM-LLMs on addressee detection, turn-change prediction, and next speaker prediction using the AMI corpus.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on the AMI corpus using accuracy and F1 scores; compared against supervised baselines (SVM, MLP) and human subjects.
card.limitation: MM-LLMs struggle to effectively leverage raw audio-visual signals; human evaluation was conducted by non-native English speakers.

slides.title: Bidirectional Tutoring for Developmental Motor Learning in Robots: Co-Developed Interaction Dynamics Support Stable Learning
slides.tldr: BIDIRECTIONAL TUTORING FOR ROBOT MOTOR LEARNING
slides.highlight: This research demonstrates that bidirectional tutoring between a robot and a tutor fosters more consistent behavioral patterns and stable motor learning than unidirectional interaction. This is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and AI-mediated embodied learning.

card.one_liner: Bidirectional tutoring improves robot motor learning by co-developing trajectories that preserve behavioral coherence and generalization.
card.key_idea: A FEP-based neural network (PV-RNN) with generative replay learns from interactive tutoring, where tutor interventions couple with the robot's prior sensorimotor dynamics.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on a humanoid robot performing object manipulation across 10 phases; bidirectional tutoring achieved significantly higher success rates (up to 90%) than unidirectional.
card.limitation: The human-tutoring experiment used only one experimenter as a tutor, limiting the assessment of variability across different human tutors.

slides.title: MuVAP: Multimodal Multiparty Voice Activity Projection for Turn-taking Prediction in the Wild
slides.highlight: MuVAP uses a causal multimodal framework to predict speaker-aware turn-taking from monaural audio and a single camera, supporting HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception and listener modeling.

card.one_liner: MuVAP predicts multiparty turn-taking using a single camera and monaural audio via role-relative projections.
card.key_idea: Grounds acoustic voice activity projections in face tracks using Role-Relative Projection, mapping N-speaker dynamics onto a fixed 'current vs. next floor-holder' state for social scalability.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on the new 31-hour AVCC dataset using Macro-F1 and accuracy for Shift-Hold and Next Speaker Prediction tasks; outperformed MLP baselines.
card.limitation: Performance is lower in 'active' prediction tasks compared to 'silent' ones and decreases as speaker count increases.

slides.title: Generating Natural and Expressive Robot Gestures through Iterative Reinforcement Learning with Human Feedback using LLMs
slides.highlight: This research uses RLHF and LLMs to improve the naturalness and expressiveness of co-speech gestures in humanoid robots, contributing to the goals of RwB regarding human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: Iterative RLHF improves the expressiveness and fluidity of LLM-generated co-speech gestures for the Pepper robot.
card.key_idea: Combines GPT-4 with a low-level motion primitive library, using Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) and few-shot prompting based on iterative human ratings to refine gesture code.
card.evaluation: Five-round online user study (250 participants) rating expressiveness, relevance, and fluidity via Likert scales; results showed statistically significant improvement over baseline (p<0.001).
card.limitation: Reliance on low-level primitives leads to repetitive patterns and mode collapse without conversation history, struggling to sustain gesture diversity.

slides.title: Beyond Usability: A UX Case Study on Using "Withdrawal Design" to Challenge Engagement Metrics in Social Robotics
slides.tldr: CHALLENGING ENGAGEMENT METRICS IN SOCIAL ROBOTICS
slides.highlight: This study examines how the removal of a social robot can prompt children with autism to seek human interaction, suggesting that high engagement may sometimes silo social behavior. This is relevant to RwB's focus on human-robot interaction and embodied social robots.

card.one_liner: Withdrawal of social robots may better promote human social motivation than continued robot engagement.
card.key_idea: A mixed-methods RCT comparing children who retained a social robot versus those who had it withdrawn to assess long-term social outcomes.
card.evaluation: N=40 home-based RCT using SCARED, RCADS, SMS, RMET, and SUS metrics; results show a trade-off between anxiety reduction and social motivation.
card.limitation: The study focuses specifically on children with autism, potentially limiting generalizability to other populations.

slides.title: Fast When, Careful Who: Dual-Process Multiparty Turn-Taking with Diffusion Augmentation
slides.highlight: This work proposes a two-stage audio-only pipeline for multiparty turn-taking that separates boundary triggering from floor transfer verification, supporting HyECHO's focus on listener modeling and engagement in hybrid teams.

card.one_liner: A dual-process audio pipeline for multiparty turn-taking using diffusion-based background augmentation to improve shift detection.
card.key_idea: A fast WavLM-based gate proposes turn boundaries, which a slow ECAPA-TDNN verifier then checks for speaker changes and predicts the next speaker.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on VoxConverse using precision, recall, F1, and MAE; compared against a ResCNN-Siamese baseline and VAP in dyadic settings.
card.limitation: Performance is constrained by boundary coverage, particularly in heavily overlapped or fast-exchange areas where acoustic cues are ambiguous.

slides.title: A Neuro-Symbolic Approach to Strategy Synthesis for Strategic Logics
slides.highlight: This work introduces a neuro-symbolic framework that uses LLMs as strategy-generation oracles validated by formal model checkers, aligning with MIMIC's use of neuro-symbolic and LLM-based agent models for societal-scale simulation.

card.one_liner: A neuro-symbolic framework using LLMs to synthesize and formally certify strategies for Natural Alternating-time Temporal Logic.
card.key_idea: A generate-and-certify architecture where an LLM proposes candidate natural strategies and a standard model checker (VITAMIN) formally validates them to ensure soundness.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on a new 4,211-instance NatATL dataset using Qwen3-32B, achieving 92% accuracy and scaling up to 50 states and 11 agents.
card.limitation: Performance is constrained by LLM token limits, which can lead to truncated outputs and parsing errors in some samples.

slides.title: WaveSync: Constrained Wavefront Optimization for Synchronized Co-Speech Gestures in Humanoid Robots
slides.tldr: SYNCHRONIZED CO-SPEECH GESTURES FOR HUMANOID ROBOTS
slides.highlight: WaveSync uses a hybrid framework and wavefront optimization to align expressive gestures with speech while ensuring kinematic feasibility. This is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: WaveSync synchronizes humanoid robot gestures with speech emphasis while respecting strict kinematic and dynamic hardware constraints.
card.key_idea: Combines LLM-generated semantic importance waves, Dynamic Movement Primitives for trajectory shaping, and a wavefront optimization module for peak-to-peak alignment and conflict resolution.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via PyBullet simulations across five scenarios using objective metrics (HbS, Jerk) and subjective Likert ratings; outperformed three ablated baselines.
card.limitation: Relies on a fixed action library, limiting its ability to handle unconstrained dialogue; not yet tested on physical hardware.
